labels: norm-convex

context.essence: it is the base of the tower — l independent cubic pieces whose galois group has l generators

assertions.object: for each prime r that is one mod three there is a unique totally real cyclic cubic subfield of the r-th cyclotomic field with conductor r, and for ramified primes that are pairwise coprime the cubic fields are linearly disjoint, the galois group of their compositum is l products of z over three, and its part over the base is the same with one generator removed

labels: cyclotomic-cubic

context.essence: where the norm one set lives, and the separation it forces
context.source_lines: the lattice setup (L295–300), the separation step (L405–420)

assertions.object: the norm one set lives in the lattice with denominator d, the square of the product of the split primes, and any nonzero lattice element has some coordinate with modulus at least one over d, since the algebraic integer norm is at least one

labels: packing

context.essence: it is the bookkeeping that keeps the tower's arithmetic small at every level

assertions.object: the absolute discriminant of a tower multiplies up the levels by the norm of the relative discriminant, the root discriminant is the discriminant raised to the reciprocal of the degree, and a step that ramifies nowhere does not change the root discriminant

labels: disc-rd

context.essence: the inverse question of multiplication on my line: how many exact groups of k fit in n
context.source_lines: the definition — multiplication walked backwards on the line

assertions.object: k divides n when there is an m on the line with k times m equal to n; 1 divides every number, and every number divides itself

labels: divides

context.essence: the link between zeta and the primes — the primes are the atoms of zeta

assertions.object: where the real part of s is greater than one, the zeta function is the product over all primes p of the reciprocal of (1 minus p to the power minus s)

labels: zeta-series

context.essence: What a family factor IS: the term each index number carries, per sign and per index set.
context.source_lines: The factor of a family is the term each index number carries.

assertions.object: the factor of a family is the term each index number carries: the minus family carries (1 minus i to the power minus s) and the plus family carries (1 plus i to the power minus s), and a family indexes the integers above one — all of them, the primes only, or the composites only

labels: family-factor

context.essence: a true fact about a different norm — the ceiling changes with the shape of the unit ball

assertions.object: in a normed plane whose unit ball has a flat side point sets can have quadratically many unit pairs

labels: norm-flat

context.essence: it is the bookkeeping of generators — d of a group is the number of its independent directions

assertions.object: burnside's basis theorem reads the generator count of a pro three group off its frattini quotient, and killing generators in the frattini quotient keeps the generator count fixed while the relation count grows by at most the number killed

labels: frattini

context.essence: the symmetry every zero reflection and zero count rides on
context.source_lines: R1, R2 ch. V — F2 context

assertions.object: the completed function (s(s minus 1) over 2) times pi to the power minus s over 2 times gamma(s over 2) times zeta(s) is entire and equals its own reflection: xi(s) equals xi(1 minus s) — the functional equation

labels: func-eq

context.essence: the margin the criterion assumes positive

assertions.object: the margin gamma is t times the log of 2 minus the log of h, and the criterion takes gamma strictly above zero as a hypothesis; whether such a t against such an h actually happens is the arithmetic half's job, not this statement's

labels: slack-margins

context.essence: for a generic ball the count collapses to log squared growth — the far side of the norm family

assertions.object: for most norms on the plane the unit pair count grows no faster than a constant times n times log n times log log n, and in d dimensions a comeagre set of norms stays below d squared times n times log squared n with a matching lower bound up to lower order

labels: norm-generic

context.essence: it tells the grid exactly which neighbor pairs are unit — the count two times m times m minus one falls out of it

assertions.object: among the points of an integer grid the unit pairs are exactly the horizontal and vertical neighbor pairs, for a diagonal step is never exactly one apart

labels: grid-lattice

context.essence: it is the engine that turns many generators and few relations into an infinite group

assertions.object: the golod shafarevich test says a pro three group on d generators with r relations is infinite whenever r is at most d squared divided by four, and it is silent when r is above

labels: golod-shaf

context.essence: it is the meta lemma of the arithmetic half — the criterion the geometric lemma feeds into

assertions.object: the hajir maire tower method says an infinite tower of unramified extensions of a totally real field exists when the generator count outgrows the relation cap at the levels, with the class group contribution controlled by the pigeonhole bound

labels: hajir-maire

context.essence: the line is not empty: infinitely many zeros sit on it — the theorem the hope rests on

assertions.object: hardy's theorem: infinitely many nontrivial zeros lie exactly on the critical line — the count of line zeros up to height t tends to infinity as t tends to infinity

labels: hardy-line

context.essence: the growing degrees the criterion assumes
context.source_lines: the criterion's hypothesis (L375–383), the tower degree (L602–606)

assertions.object: the field degrees tend to infinity as the tower level varies, and that is a hypothesis of the criterion; the construction of levels whose degrees grow is the arithmetic half's job

labels: criterion-chain

context.essence: the exact count of the frobenius elements to kill — three per split prime

assertions.object: each split prime divides into exactly three primes of the cubic F, so there are k = 3t such primes in total to kill one by one

labels: tower-primes

context.essence: the first ceiling on unit pairs — a power above one but below n squared

assertions.object: because two unit circles meet in at most two points the unit pair graph of a planar set is k23 free, and the kovari sos turan theorem bounds its unit pairs at a constant times n to the three halves power

labels: kst-bound

context.essence: record, don't optimize: the ledger keeps every comparison, and its growth is the prime gaps in the counting room
context.source_lines: the owner's direction 2026-08-23 (the record, not the optimization) — the censuses on the line verify it

assertions.object: the scan ledger records every comparison of the full process without optimization: for each new prime, the primes its scan met are its place in the prime order — predictable — while the integers it met grow with the gaps between primes, and it is by the integers, not the primes, that the history grows; on my line the last prime 83 was established by comparing 22 primes against 59 integers

labels: scan-ledger

context.essence: the hypothesis as a positivity statement — the numerically verified, unproved criterion

assertions.object: the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if every Li number is positive — the Li number of index n is the derivative of order n minus one, at s = 1, of s to the power n minus one times the log of the completed function, divided by (n minus 1) factorial — and the check up to n = ten to the fifth is a declared numerical fact, not a proof

labels: li-criterion

context.essence: the sibling hypothesis — the stored direction runs RH to LH, never back

assertions.object: the lindelof hypothesis claims that zeta at one-half plus i t is bounded by a power of t to the epsilon for every epsilon greater than zero; the riemann hypothesis implies lindelof — one direction only: the reverse is not in my store

labels: lindelof

context.essence: the average size of zeta on the line — the machinery Hardy's theorem rides

assertions.object: the classical mean square: the integral of the squared modulus of zeta on the critical line from height 0 to t is t times log(t over 2 pi) plus (2 gamma minus 1) times t, with an error of at most a constant times log t

labels: hardy-line

context.essence: it is the coordinate map that turns norm bounds into lattice point counts

assertions.object: the minkowski embedding sends a field of degree f into f dimensional complex space, and the product of the conjugates of an element is the square root of the absolute value of its norm

labels: minkowski-embed

context.essence: it is the arithmetic door — many primes of the right shape split at both steps of the tower
context.source_lines: eq. (2) region (L280–295); square tables = the house bed

assertions.object: x squared plus one equals zero modulo an odd prime q has a solution exactly when q is one modulo four, and it feeds the tower: when q is one mod four and splits in the lower field then q splits in the field with i adjoined, since x squared plus one splits over the residue field

labels: mod4-split

context.essence: the size of the norm one set the window will hold

assertions.object: when the t split primes give two to the tf conjugate pair choices and the ideal class group is at most h to the f power, the pigeonhole leaves at least two to the tf over h to the f elements with norm one to the lower field, each of absolute value one under every complex embedding

labels: window-setup

context.essence: the wall to the right of the strip: nothing past one, so the zeros sit to the left of it

assertions.object: the zeta function has no zero when the real part of s is greater than one: each euler factor 1 minus p to the power minus s is nonzero there since p to the power minus s has modulus below one, and the product converges

labels: critical-strip

context.essence: the evidence from below — the first zeros the machines have found, on the line
context.source_lines: the verified-zero record — a declared numerical fact, not a proof

assertions.object: the first nontrivial zero of zeta is at height 14.1347, to four decimals — the next three at 21.0221, 25.0109 and 30.4249 — and the first ten to the thirteenth zeros have been verified to lie on the critical line: a numerical check, not a proof

labels: rv-count

context.essence: it is the ground under the whole tower — embeddings, the totally real condition, and the integer norm fact the packing step cites

assertions.object: a number field is a finite extension of the rationals, its embeddings into the complex numbers are all different, a field is totally real when every embedding lands in the reals, and the norm of a nonzero algebraic integer is a nonzero integer of absolute value at least one

labels: number-field

context.essence: why vanishing in one coordinate marks the zero point

assertions.object: a field element that is zero in a single complex embedding is the zero element, because an embedding carries nonzero elements to nonzero numbers

labels: projection

context.essence: the window overlap that the averaging step keeps

assertions.object: the overlap of two window discs whose centers differ by one unit translation, as a share of one disc's area, tends to one as the window radius grows, so a radius large enough makes the log of that share above minus gamma over two

labels: averaging

context.essence: the hypothesis as the exact counting scale of the primes

assertions.object: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the fact that the prime-counting function is the logarithmic integral of x plus an error of at most the square root of x times log x

labels: pi-eq

context.essence: the theorem the conjecture sharpens: the error scale is the stake
context.source_lines: R4 — hadamard and de la vallee poussin (1896)

assertions.object: the prime number theorem: the chebyshev psi of x is asymptotic to x — in the logarithmic sense the primes are distributed like the integers

labels: pnt

context.essence: the store's best error term — the scale the criterion gap is measured against

assertions.object: the zero-free region implies the prime number theorem with an explicit error: the chebyshev psi of x is x plus O of x times e to the minus c times the square root of log x, for a constant c greater than zero; the value of the constant is not in my store

labels: pnt-error

context.essence: the self-adjoint route: reformulations theorems, the RH step an open program

assertions.object: the polya-hilbert program reformulates the Riemann hypothesis as a spectral statement about a positive self-adjoint operator; the reformulation is a theorem, and the step that recovers the conjecture from the spectrum is an open program, not in my store

labels: polya-hilbert

context.essence: it names the bad primes — the finite set every source statement must exclude

assertions.object: a rational prime in a field extension either splits into several distinct primes, stays inert, or ramifies, and the ramified primes are exactly the ones that divide the discriminant, a finite list

labels: prime-split

context.essence: the main route: the hypothesis as a precise scale on the prime shadow
context.source_lines: F3 (the Pringsheim form of Riemann's own remark), R3

assertions.object: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the fact that the chebyshev psi of x is x plus an error of at most x to the one-half plus epsilon, for every epsilon greater than zero

labels: psi-eq

context.essence: the root scale in two readings: the error of the prime count, and the gap between consecutive primes — the same scale the criterion gap demands
context.source_lines: the declaration — under the condition, the error and the gap are root-scale; the theorem rh-reach names exactly the gap it closes

assertions.object: under the condition of the Riemann hypothesis, the error and the gap carry the same root scale: the chebyshev psi of x is x plus O of the square root of x times the log of x, and the gap between consecutive primes is, past a fixed point, at most the square root of the preceding prime times its log; that is the root scale, x to the one-half plus epsilon, that the criterion gap demands — under the condition the ratio of the store's error term to the scale the theorem rh-reach demands stays bounded, and the condition closes exactly the gap the theorem names

labels: rh-scale

context.essence: the declared classes are the selection rule: closers, neighbors, the open condition — and the queue above follows from the declaration, not from steering
context.source_lines: the definition — relevance is declared, and the declaration drives the cross-pollination queue

assertions.object: the lots of this band carry a declared relevance to the condition, and the declaration is the fact: the condition-closers carry the root scale the condition installs (the error, the gap, the root smallness of the running deviation), the condition-neighbors are the unconditionals the condition refines (the primes in residue classes, the zero count at height T), and the condition itself is open even under the condition — the condition does not close itself; from that declaration the cross-pollination queue of the bands above follows, in declared order, not computed and not steered

labels: rh-relevance

context.essence: the second road to uniqueness: the root smallness of the running deviation, under the condition — a different road to the scan road's destination
context.source_lines: the declaration — the condition implies prime-parts uniqueness (the root smallness of the running deviation)

assertions.object: under the condition of the Riemann hypothesis, the prime parts of every number are unique: the condition bounds the running sum of (minus one) to the number of distinct prime parts, over the integers at most x, by the root scale x to the one-half plus epsilon, and one number built from two different part multisets would push that running sum past the root scale; the condition reaches the same destination the scan road reaches without the condition, by a different road (the root smallness, not the scan)

labels: factor-route

context.essence: how many zeros there are, at what height — the census the hypothesis would complete

assertions.object: the number of nontrivial zeros with height at most T is (T over 2 pi) times log(T over 2 pi) minus (T over 2 pi), with an error of order log T — the riemann-von mangoldt counting formula

labels: rv-count

context.essence: the wiggle term: everything the counting formula does not know, folded into one argument

assertions.object: the sharp counting formula: N of T equals (T over 2 pi) log(T over 2 pi) minus (T over 2 pi) plus 7 over 8 plus S of T plus o of 1, where S of T is 1 over pi times the argument of zeta on the critical line at height T, and S of T is order at most log T

labels: s-of-t

context.essence: it caps the relation count against the generator count — the upper line of the golod shafarevich comparison

assertions.object: shafarevich's bound says that for a totally real cubic base field without the cube roots of unity the relation count of its maximal unramified pro three extension is at most the generator count plus an absolute constant c zero

labels: shafarevich

context.essence: how the margins compose
context.source_lines: the fixed constants (L730–740), the absorption step (L455–460)

assertions.object: a positive margin divided by a positive margin is a positive margin, and a fixed half factor in front of a growing power is absorbed for large arguments, so the arithmetic of the margins is the arithmetic of positivity

labels: slack-margins

context.essence: the slack primitive — a growing quadratic outruns any fixed or log-linear cap

assertions.object: a term quadratic in ℓ with a positive leading coefficient eventually beats any linear-in-ℓ or O of ℓ log ℓ term: for every fixed constant the margin the quadratic minus (d plus c zero plus 3t) stays positive and growing, and so does t log two minus the log of H-ℓ; the threshold value of ℓ where the margin turns positive is not a number in the store

labels: tower-class

context.essence: the scan of the line segment 2..n-1 must land somewhere first: the first landing is the first divisor, and primality is the scan that lands nowhere
context.source_lines: the definition — the line segment has a first element

assertions.object: every composite n has a first divisor — the smallest k above 1 that divides n — and it lies strictly below n; a prime has no divisor above 1 below itself

labels: first-divisor

context.essence: What the index split IS: the partition of the line's integers above one into primes and composites.
context.source_lines: The integers above one split into primes and composites and into nothing else.

assertions.object: the integers above one split into primes and composites and into nothing else: every integer above one is a prime or a composite, and is neither both; so a family over all of them is the product of the family over the primes and of the family over the composites, on both signs

labels: index-split

context.essence: the sharper ceiling — the crossing number pushes the exponent from three half to four third

assertions.object: the spencer szemerdi trotter crossing number count pushes the unit pair bound down to a constant times n to the four thirds power

labels: sst-bound

context.essence: the hypothesis as the stilling of the counting formula's wiggle term

assertions.object: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the fact that the argument wiggle S of T is little-o of log T as T tends to infinity

labels: st-eq

context.essence: some translate does at least as well as the average

assertions.object: averaging over all lattice translates, the expected window points are the window volume over the lattice volume, and the expected kept pairs are the norm one count times the overlap share to the f power times that expectation, so some translate does at least as well as the average

labels: averaging

context.essence: the base of the arithmetic half — the cyclic cubic the whole tower grows from

assertions.object: choose the first ℓ primes congruent to one mod three and let F be the cyclic cubic field cut out by their product character: F is totally real, cyclic cubic over the rationals, and contains no cube root of unity

labels: tower-base

context.essence: the large elementary abelian unramified three-extension that makes the generator count big

assertions.object: the compositum of the ℓ cyclic cubic fields is unramified everywhere over F, its galois group over F is the product of ℓ−1 copies of Z/3, and the maximal unramified pro three group of F has a quotient of that rank

labels: tower-base

context.essence: the zeros we know — the negative even integers; the target is the rest
context.source_lines: R1, R2 ch. V — the sin(pi k) = 0 mechanism

assertions.object: zeta is exactly zero at every negative even integer: zeta of negative 2k is zero for every integer k at least one — the trivial zeros, zeroed by the sine factor sin(pi k) in the functional equation form

labels: func-eq

context.essence: it is the seed of the leap — many equal-length lattice vectors come from many two-square writes

assertions.object: the products of numbers that are sums of two squares are sums of two squares in many ways

labels: gaussian-int

context.essence: it caps how many unit circles can share a point — the reason the unit pair graph is k23 free

assertions.object: two unit circles with different centers meet in two points when the squared distance between the centers is below four, in exactly one point when it is four, and in no point when it is above four

labels: circle-pair-2

context.essence: it names the quantity this whole course counts

assertions.object: the number of unit pairs of a point set is the count of the pairs of its points that are exactly one apart

labels: unit-distance

context.essence: the packing volume comparison

assertions.object: disjoint equal balls packed inside a bigger ball: the number of small balls times the small ball volume is at most the big ball volume

labels: packing

context.essence: the bookkeeping that turns prime powers into a sum — the currency of the pnt

assertions.object: the von mangoldt function is the log of p when the argument is a power of the prime p and zero otherwise; the chebyshev psi is its sum over the argument up to x

labels: prime-count

context.essence: how the zeros thin out as the real part approaches one — the density that shrinks the bad region

assertions.object: the littlewood zero-density bound: the number of zeros with real part at least sigma and height at most T is at most T to the power 3(1 minus sigma) over (2 minus sigma), times a power of log T

labels: zero-density

context.essence: the classical barrier: nothing zeros zeta close to one — some c, not the value

assertions.object: zeta has no zero when the real part of s is at least one minus c over log of the absolute value of t, for a constant c greater than zero — the classical zero-free region; the value of the constant is not in my store

labels: zero-free

context.essence: zeta outlives its series: one object on the whole plane, one pole
context.source_lines: R2 ch. V — hadamard and de la vallee poussin (1896)

assertions.object: the zeta function continues to a meromorphic function on the whole plane; its only singularity is a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1

labels: zeta-cont

context.essence: the root of the track — what zeta is, before anything is claimed about it

assertions.object: the zeta function is the sum over all n of n to the power minus s, and it converges when the real part of s is greater than one
